A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIDE/Chameleon study, and all supplied pages are readable. v1 includes Appendices A–B; v2 ends with references and contains no appendices despite retaining references to them. These omissions are directly observable, rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original AIDE benchmark results, perturbation experiments and component ablations in Tables 2–6, plus AP results in Appendix B/Table 8.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, robustness and ablation results in Tables 3–7 and adds qualitative component-ablation examples in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Figure 2 and the method description retain DCT-based patch selection, SRM filtering, two ResNet-50 branches, OpenCLIP semantic features and MLP fusion. No procedural redesign is established; the inconsistent rewritten fusion equation does not demonstrate an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIGCDetectBenchmark, GenImage and Chameleon, retaining the same generator coverage, Chameleon categories and reported image counts. JPEG compression and Gaussian-blur scenarios also remain. The new dataset-comparison table and qualitative examples do not establish additional task or population coverage.

E2.justification: In the B1 accuracy comparison, v2 adds NPR and removes GramNet. In the Chameleon comparison, NPR replaces LGrad, while GramNet remains. GenImage and perturbation-test comparator sets are unchanged; the revised general detector list does not accurately describe every table's membership.

E3.justification: Chameleon's aggregate accuracy changes from equal-class averaging to values generally consistent with weighting by the 14,863 real and 11,170 fake images. For example, CNNSpot's ProGAN-trained aggregate changes from 49.88 to 56.94 despite identical class accuracies. This aggregation revision is unexplained. Retained training budgets and perturbation settings agree.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 provides qualitative cases showing errors when either semantic or patchwise features are omitted, supplementing the component analysis. The seven quantitative ablation configurations and JPEG/blur robustness experiments retain their previous results; their renumbering does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Both present point estimates without uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Chameleon results and rankings change substantially. Under All GenImage, AIDE changes from 58.73 to 63.89 and UnivFD from 63.54 to 60.42 despite unchanged class-specific scores; this is an aggregation-induced ranking reversal, not a comparable-metric performance gain. SD-trained AIDE's fake/real accuracies change from 40.61/82.46 to 16.82/94.38, and CNNSpot's fake accuracy from 13.86 to 8.86. NPR results are added, some comparator entries disappear, and the entire AP table is omitted. B1 AIDE's ADM accuracy also changes from 93.45 to 93.43. GenImage, robustness and quantitative ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Most mathematical definitions and computations are retained or redisplayed. However, after defining Fmean as the average of the two patch features, v2 Equation (8) introduces an additional, malformed avgpool expression involving Fmean and the semantic feature. This conflicts with v1's concatenation formula and the retained prose. It is a localized mathematical-specification error; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: Chameleon exposes weaknesses in existing detectors, and AIDE combines patch statistics with semantic features. The claimed 3.5- and 4.6-point benchmark improvements and the acknowledgment that realistic image detection remains unsolved are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific explanations connecting ablation failures to high-frequency smoothness, low-frequency noise and semantic artifacts. It also adds Chameleon-specific misuse concerns and argues that dataset magnitude and resolution increase evaluation difficulty. v1's AP-based interpretation concerning performance across thresholds disappears, while the limitation of poor Chameleon performance remains.

D1.justification: Implementation settings move unchanged from v1 Appendix A.1 into v2 Section 5.1. v2 newly specifies two independent annotators with unanimous realism judgments, image licensing or permission requirements, and planned EULA approval for dataset access. A project homepage replaces the repository-release announcement. Conversely, explicit training sample counts and the distinction between the two BigGAN test sets are omitted with the detailed benchmark documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds the NPR reference, Tan et al. (2024), and removes works including the single-patch detector, the JPEG-bias study and Diffusion Noise Feature, alongside several dataset-source references. The related-work narrative largely remains. The new dataset comparison additionally positions Chameleon as the first real-life evaluation dataset and the most extensive collection.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: detailed benchmark descriptions are replaced by a compact dataset paragraph, implementation details move into the main text, and the appendix structure disappears. Comparison, robustness and ablation prose is rewritten, with ablations reorganized around individual modules. Dataset-comparison and societal-impact passages are added, and Architecture becomes Methodology.

P2.justification: The B1 accuracy table is transposed and loses its GAN/DM summary rows. A new dataset-comparison table reworks part of v1's appendix statistics, Figure 4 adds qualitative examples, and the AP table disappears. Radar plots, captions and table highlighting are revised, alongside a document-wide template change. Figures 1–2 largely retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: NPR comparisons, qualitative examples and annotation/licensing disclosures are useful additions. However, v2 removes all AP evidence and important benchmark details while still directing readers to an absent appendix, and it leaves the ranking-changing Chameleon aggregation revision unexplained. Its new size comparison also places Chameleon's total image count alongside counts explicitly identified as fake-only in v1 Table 7, undermining the 'most extensive' claim. These losses modestly outweigh the additions in evidential clarity and reproducibility, while the core method and most experiments remain intact.
